newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Singapore business eyes S.African opportunities.
newsitem.headline: Singapore business eyes S.African opportunities.

text.p: High-profile Singapore business representatives currently visiting South Africa are likely to enter joint venture partnerships with local firms, business delegation leader Chandra Das said on Wednesday.

"We are confident that there are new investment opportunities and will assess what is possible...the type of investments we are looking at are likely to be joint venture partnerships," Das told a news briefing hosted by Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd.
While no definite business ventures have yet been concluded, one member of the delegation had already signed an agreement to buy property in Cape Town to develop a hotel, he said.
The delegation arrived in South Africa on Monday to accompany Singapore's Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong who held talks with President Nelson Mandela in Cape Town on Tuesday.
Tong urged South Africa to take advantage of its position to become a regional hub for travel and trade.
The team is not the first to visit South Africa but it is the largest to come out of Singapore so far, with 41 members representing 36 organisations, Das said.
"The aim is to meet influential South African business people to talk about mergers, acquisitions and investments into South Africa," he said.
The development of South Africa's infrastructure is one of the main areas of focus, Das said.

Deputy President of the Development Bank of Singapore Ltd, Tan Soo Nan, said problem areas identified by foreign investors coming into South Africa were crime, the exchange rate and the high interest rate environment.
"There are problem areas that will have to be considered from the point of view of a foreign investor," he said.
From South Africa, the Singapore business team will move on Zimbabwe, Namibia and Botswana for similar exploratory investment talks.
